correctness.rationale: For a strictly ordered two-class mixture, common denominators give odds x(x+c)/(P+dx), with c=wb+(1−w)a, d=wa+(1−w)b, P=ab and cd−P=w(1−w)(b−a)^2>0. A convenient independent check of the minimum uses m=√(cP/d), r=√(cd/P)>1 and x=m exp(t): the log-slope is 1−(r²−1)/(1+r²+2r cosh(t)), uniquely minimized at t=0 with h=2/(1+r). Consequently c=rm and d=rP/m are forced. Fixing the odds to one at z then gives the stated strictly positive P. Conversely any admitted m,h,z yields cd>P; the quadratic with sum c+d and product P has distinct positive roots and is negative at c, placing c strictly between the roots and the weight strictly between zero and one. This reconstructs the curve and all three summaries, with the intended lower-affinity-constant class weight and no hidden constraints. Since the image is the open Cartesian product, every pair leaves an entire interval of possibilities; the statement is restricted to pairs of the three named diagnostics. Equal constants and pure classes collapse to h=1 and are not asserted to be identifiable by these formulas.
residual_risks: Exact, correctly normalized equilibrium curves only. There is no discrimination among mechanisms having the same binding curve and no guarantee of practical estimability of the minimum.

value.rationale: An exact noiseless binding curve ordinarily supplies many observables. Here a fixed set of three interpretable diagnostics captures everything in the two-affinity model, while dropping any one of them leaves an actual continuum of fits. The exact feasible range and inverse therefore say which summary measurements can be discarded or retained in structural inference and provide a precise baseline for practical studies without suggesting that a subunit slope identifies mechanism.
residual_risks: No sample-size, robustness or estimation-efficiency theorem; near h=1 or in ill-conditioned parameter ranges the inversion may be impractical.
